proof_nl:
Assume the standing definitions are
F_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
and
H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Let x satisfy (n-1)/n <= x < 1.

For each k with 1 <= k < n, we have
k(n-1)/n <= kx < k,
so in fact k-1 < kx < k. Hence floor(kx) = k-1.
For k = n, we have
n-1 <= nx < n,
so floor(nx) = n-1.

Therefore
F_n(x) = (n-1) - sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (k-1)/k - (n-1)/n.
Now
sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (k-1)/k = sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (1 - 1/k) = (n-1) - sum_{k=1}^{n-1} 1/k,
so
F_n(x) = (n-1) - [(n-1) - sum_{k=1}^{n-1} 1/k] - (n-1)/n
= sum_{k=1}^{n-1} 1/k - (n-1)/n
= H_{n-1} - (n-1)/n.
Using H_n = H_{n-1} + 1/n, we get
H_{n-1} - (n-1)/n = H_n - 1.
Thus F_n(x) = H_n - 1 for every x in [(n-1)/n, 1).
solver_summary: On the interval [(n-1)/n,1), the floors are constant: floor(kx)=k-1 for k<n and floor(nx)=n-1. Substituting into F_n and simplifying gives H_n-1.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly establishes that for every x in [(n-1)/n, 1), all floor terms are fixed as claimed, and the resulting algebra simplifies to H_n - 1. The argument is complete for the stated lemma and stays within the semantic scope of the provided definitions.
